name: Client IP address
plain: Every request carries the sender's public IP address.
meaning: The server sees the IP (or the proxy or relay address). IPv4 gives about 32 bits at most; an IPv6 /64 gives up to 64. It is the base for geolocation, ISP and VPN checks, and rate limits. Shared NAT and CGNAT blur it.

web.api: TCP/IP source address; X-Forwarded-For at proxies

steps: Server reads the socket peer address
Join with GeoIP and ASN databases

limits.headline: Can see the public internet address your connection uses
limits.user_action: Nothing. Every site you visit gets it when you connect
can: See your IP address, or your VPN, proxy or relay address
Guess your country and city from it
Check your internet company and spot VPNs
Limit how many requests one address can make
cannot: Find your street address or name
See your device's private home network address
Be sure it is you; shared connections and carrier networks blur it

story.what_it_is: Every site you visit sees your internet address.
story.for_you: You never see it, but every site you visit receives your network address. It shows your internet provider and rough area. A VPN or relay swaps it for another address.
story.for_makers: Makers need it to send you the page. They also use it for rough location, rate limits, abuse blocking and fraud, and ads use it to link visits from the same home or office.

use_cases.example: A multiplayer game server uses your address to place you in a region and connect you with nearby players.
A cloud gaming service uses your address to pick the closest data center for the lowest lag.
A streaming service uses it to decide which shows are licensed in your country.
A website blocks an address that tries a password thousands of times.
An ad network links visits from one household address to guess that devices belong together.
A site counts unique visitors and cities by address.
A bank flags a login from an address it has never seen for that customer.

technical_bounds: Hidden by VPN, Tor, iCloud Private Relay, Chrome IP Protection and corporate proxies
CGNAT shares one IP among hundreds of users

value.legit_uses: Rate limiting, abuse prevention, geo compliance
value.abuse: Cross-site tracking when combined with other signals
